calls.label: Why three wires
calls.says: Why are there three wires, and why does the black one matter?
calls.reply: Three wires because the sensor needs three different jobs done — one carries power in, one carries the reading out, and the black one carries it back home so the circuit actually completes. Without a way home, the electricity has nowhere to go and nothing works, even if the other two are perfect. Right now you're on the pull-the-yellow-wire step — has the number on the display done anything since you pulled it?

calls.label: Why three wires
calls.says: Why are there three wires, and why does the black one matter?
calls.reply: Three jobs, three wires: red brings power to sensor A, yellow carries the reading back, and black gives the current a way home to the board — without it the circuit isn't actually a loop, just a dead end. Right now you're on step 07, pulling the yellow one out on purpose — has the display changed since you did that?

Three wires because the sensor needs three different jobs done: the red one brings power in, the yellow one carries the reading out, and the black one is ground — the path the current takes back home to finish the circuit.
